source.title: James Bond Style Explained | How to Dress Like 007

tips.text: Aim to look exceptionally well dressed while seeming barely to have tried: precise, understated clothes with no unnecessary details.
A navy polo with a substantial collar, minimal branding and a fit that follows the body without clinging is one of the most useful casual pieces.
tips.why: It sits between a tee and a shirt and goes with chinos, grey trousers or dark denim.

tips.text: A cheap piece that fits beautifully beats an expensive one that fits badly.
tips.why: Fit makes far more visual difference than price.

tips.text: Stick to a restrained palette of navy, grey, black and camel or other earthy neutrals so nearly everything combines.
tips.why: A limited palette multiplies outfits without adding clothes.

tips.text: Choose clothes for your own build rather than copying a celebrity's exact cut; slimmer, broader or shorter men need different proportions.
tips.why: The goal is the effect, not someone else's measurements.

tips.text: Hemming trousers and correcting sleeve lengths makes inexpensive clothes look more expensive than untouched designer pieces.
With a muted palette, keep outfits interesting through texture: waxed cotton, wool, suede, leather, denim and cashmere together.
tips.why: Mixed materials add depth without loud colour.

tips.text: A navy sweater with navy trousers can look flat; with dark denim and suede boots it comes alive.
tips.why: Contrasting materials break up one colour.

tips.text: A Harrington, simple bomber or lightweight blouson over a polo and jeans makes a timeless urban casual look; the silhouette matters more than the label.
tips.why: Clean short jackets suit everyday wear.

tips.text: Dress for the setting: a rugged knit in the countryside, a polo and light trousers in the heat, a linen shirt in summer.
tips.why: Clothes that suit the place look intentional.

tips.text: A clean polo, chinos and loafers or suede shoes is the ideal middle ground between sloppy and formal.
tips.why: Casual clothes held to formal standards of fit.

tips.text: Suede chukkas bridge rugged and refined: smarter than sneakers, less formal than dress shoes, and they go with almost any trousers.
A few versatile shoes cover most needs: dark chukkas, dark leather boots, clean minimal sneakers and a pair of loafers.
tips.why: Shoes that cross categories save money.

tips.text: Spend selectively: more on a jacket, coat or boots you'll wear for years, less on basic T-shirts.
tips.why: Quality matters most where wear is heaviest.

tips.text: Don't wear every piece associated with a style icon at once; the result looks like cosplay.
tips.why: Subtle inspiration looks stylish; a full copy looks like a costume.
